payload.name: Extract_Explicit_User_Preference
payload.description: When a user explicitly states a favorite or strong preference (e.g., 'X is my favorite', 'Definitely X!'), during extraction, always create a preference candidate even if the message already produced other candidates.
content: During candidate extraction, if a user utterance contains an explicit first-person preference statement naming an item (e.g., 'Definitely X! It's my favorite'), always emit a preference memory candidate for that item, regardless of how many other candidates the message yields.
Do not require the preference to be the message's main topic; a clause or exclamation is sufficient.
Do not apply to hypotheticals, negated statements, or preferences expressed about other people.

solves: The general failure is that extraction can skip a clearly stated user preference when it appears in a message that already yielded other candidates or when it is phrased as an exclamation. The skill applies to any future session where a user explicitly names an item as their favorite or strongly preferred; it does not apply to implicit likes, negations, or statements about other people's preferences, where the base extraction judgment remains sufficient.
